session_note: The 126th South Carolina General Assembly covers the full 2025-2026 biennium as one continuous session (scstatehouse.gov groups all bill pages under a single 'sess126_2025-2026' folder with one continuous bill-number sequence). Confirmed directly from the legislature's own bill pages: the 2nd regular session of the 126th General Assembly convened 2026-01-13, and bills prefiled in December 2025 (e.g., H.4583, S.724) were simply 'introduced and read first time' on that date under the same bill number with no reintroduction, demonstrating that 2025-2026 carryover requires no procedural restart. I could not retrieve a scstatehouse.gov page that states the exact 2026 sine die adjournment date in so many words (the site's code/constitution chapters I fetched did not contain it, its bill-search and subject-search tools require form POSTs that WebFetch could not execute, and WebSearch was unavailable - this session's search budget was already exhausted before this task began). South Carolina's regular session is widely understood to be governed by a mandatory sine die rule of the second Thursday in May (S.C. Code 2-1-180), which for 2026 falls on 2026-05-14; this is circumstantially corroborated by the bill-history evidence below, since none of the 7 tracked bills shows any action after 2026-05-06, consistent with the regular session having concluded around that date with no floor votes reached on any of them. Because the 126th General Assembly's term does not end until the 127th General Assembly organizes in January 2027, none of these bills is dead: each remains a live, pending bill in its committee of referral and could still be acted on if the chambers return for any special/interim business or when session resumes, and only formally dies if unpassed by the true end of the 2025-2026 term. Given the ambiguity between 'still in committee during an active session' versus 'session recessed post sine die but bill still pending,' I used bill_status_category 'in_committee' for all bills below (directly supported by each fetched bill page, which shows the bill still assigned to a committee with no floor vote), and flagged the carryover/non-death point in each bill's notes rather than asserting a category the schema might read as more final.
